en: The Ritual Manual for the *Dhāraṇī of the Flaming Mouth* from the Essential Compendium of Yoga for Saving Ānanda,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra by Imperial Decree during the Tang Dynasty.
At that time, the World-Honored One was at the Nyagrodha Monastery in the city of Kāla,
together with a vast assembly of bhikṣus and innumerable bodhisattvas.
He sat surrounded by his followers and preached the Dharma to them.
At that time, Ānanda was dwelling alone in a quiet place, reflecting upon the teachings he had received.
Then, after the third watch of the night had passed, he—
He saw a hungry ghost named Yānmouth (Yamamukha),
whose form was hideous and whose body was withered and emaciated;
fire blazed from his mouth, and his throat was as narrow as the point of a needle.
With disheveled hair and long, sharp teeth and claws,
he was most terrifying;
standing before Ānanda, he addressed him, saying:
"Three days from now, your life will come to an end,
and you will immediately be reborn among the hungry ghosts.
When Ānanda heard these words, he...
His heart filled with terror, he asked the hungry ghost:
"Great Being, if after my death I am reborn as a hungry ghost,
what skillful means should I now practice to escape this suffering?"
At that time, the hungry ghosts said to Ānanda,
"If on the coming day at dawn you can provide food and drink as an act of charity for hundreds of thousands of nayutas of hungry ghosts, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River..."
Furthermore, it includes the food and drink consumed by immeasurable other brahmin seers, the officials of the underworld presided over by Yama,
various spirits and ghosts, and those who have long since passed away.
"According to the measure used in the kingdom of Magadha,
provide seventy-seven measures of food and drink for each,
and on our behalf, make offerings to the Triple Gem."
"You have gained increased longevity,
and you have enabled us to escape the sufferings of the hungry ghosts and be reborn in the heavens.
Ānanda saw this hungry ghost with the flaming mouth.
His body was emaciated, withered, and extremely hideous;
fire blazed from his mouth and his throat was like a needle;
his hair was disheveled and tangled, and his fur and claws were long and sharp.
Furthermore, hearing these bitter words, he was greatly terrified and his hair stood on end.
Immediately at dawn, he rose from his seat and went to where the Buddha was,
circumambulating him three times to the right.
Prostrating at the Buddha’s feet with his body trembling, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O World-Honored One of Great Compassion, I pray that you will save me from my suffering.
Why is this? Last night, during the third watch,"
While walking in meditation at a quiet place, he recollected the Dharma he had received.
He then saw the Yama-mouth ghost, who spoke to him, saying:
"In three days, your life will surely come to an end, and you shall be reborn among the hungry ghosts."
I asked the hungry ghost, "How may I escape this suffering?
The hungry ghost replied, "If you can give alms to as many immeasurable hungry ghosts as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of Ganges Rivers..."
The Brahman seer Yama, the presiding official over the paths of karma, the dark-world functionaries,
along with their various ghosts, spirits, attendants, and retinues,
as well as those who have passed away long ago.
He bestowed food and drink equally upon all hungry ghosts.
Your life-span increased, and you addressed the World-Honored One, saying, "How can one provide such immeasurable food and drink as to satisfy them all?
The Buddha told Ānanda, "Do not be afraid now."
I recall that in the past, during immeasurable kalpas, when I was once a brahmin,
I received from the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara a dhāraṇī called the "Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata of Immeasurable Majestic Virtue, Sovereignty, and Radiance."
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"If you are well able to perform this dhāraṇī rite seven times with empowerment,
you can cause a single meal to transform into various kinds of ambrosial food and drink."
He was immediately able to satisfy hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of hungry ghosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
as well as brāhmaṇas, rishis, and various classes of spirits and deities,
so that they all obtained excellent food and drink and were fully satiated.
Each member of this assembly likewise obtained a *droṇa* measure used in the kingdom of Magadha;
this food and this water were equal in volume to the Dharma-realm, and though they ate, it was inexhaustible.
All have attained the fruits of sainthood and liberated their bodies from suffering.
The Buddha told Ānanda: "From now on, you shall receive and uphold this dharani method;
it will cause your merit, virtue, and lifespan to increase."
If hungry ghosts are reborn in the heavens or pure lands and receive the bodies of humans or devas,
they can cause the donor to transform obstacles, eliminate calamities, prolong their years, and increase their lifespan;
they will manifest superior merit in the present and realize Bodhi in the future.
Having generated the vast and great mind for the universal benefit of all sentient beings,
one considers that throughout many kalpas since time immemorial, they have been one's parents;
whether among the constellations, the celestial bureaus, the dark offices, or the earthly prisons.
All sentient beings, including those in the realm of Yama and the world of ghosts, as well as all wriggling and crawling creatures, gathered for a universal and unobstructed great offering.
Riding upon the Buddha’s majestic radiance, they purified their physical fields.
Having attained this victory, one enjoys the bliss of humans and devas.
I pray that all Buddhas, Prajñāpāramitā, Bodhisattvas, Vajradevas,
and all the immeasurable sages of the paths of karma may [be favorable].
We realize our practice through unconditioned compassion (*nirālamba-maitrī*).
Therefore, desiring to fulfill our great vows, and wishing to provide vast protection so that sentient beings may be rescued and not fall back, we act accordingly.
It is for the purpose of destroying all karmas so that they may be purified;
it is because one desires to seek the unsurpassed path with diligence so as to achieve swift accomplishment;
and it is because one desires to rescue and deliver sentient beings from the evil realms.
Because they have forever cast off the ocean of suffering and ascended to the other shore.
As stated in the sutras, regarding all those who act as sovereigns,
rulers, and leaders among the six realms of existence and four modes of birth within the boundless worlds:
All of these are manifestations of the compassionate vows of Bodhisattvas dwelling in the inconceivable liberation;
they divide their forms and spread their shadows, manifesting transformation bodies that undergo suffering alongside those of their own kind within the six realms of existence.
Even when employing skillful means, they are not corrupted by afflictions or secondary afflictions;
they discern various karmas to inspire the aspiration for the Way,
and constantly reproach themselves, repenting of the deeds committed by their own bodies.
He tames and transforms all sentient beings;
as a great guide, he destroys the three miserable realms,
purifies the paths of karma, and cuts off the flow of craving.
Without abandoning their conduct and vows, they remain within the ocean of suffering as spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
They bring all sentient beings to maturity for their benefit and happiness, leading them to realize great *nirvāṇa*.
If there are donors who have deep faith in the Mahāyāna and a yearning aspiration for Yoga, [they should...]
They aspire to see and hear the nectar-like Dharma gateway of the *dhāraṇī-piṭaka*;
they give rise to a mind of rescue and deliverance for all sentient beings;
and with earnest devotion, they praise the relinquishing of great wealth and treasures.
After he had requested it three times from his teacher, the latter finally permitted him to practice the dharma of giving (*dāna*).
With equanimity and uniformity, free from thoughts of enmity or aversion,
he constantly practiced generosity without any regret.
They draw near to virtuous friends and apply themselves with courageous diligence;
free from cowardice, they seek the Great Way,
extol the Triple Gem, and cherish all living beings.
They employ skillful means to rescue and deliver all beings, causing them to attain liberation.
They do not sustain their own bodies or lives through evil pursuits,
but constantly benefit both themselves and others.
That son of good family is a true and virtuous friend who practices the bodhisattva path for the sake of all beings within the three miserable realms and the various evil destinies.
All the hungry ghosts, the Lord of the Fiery Hell (Yama-rāja),
and others; the Brahmins, the sages, the various devas of the void,
Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Heavenly Kings, and the celestial bureaus of the lunar mansions.
The eight classes of nāgas and devas, the sun, moon, and Mount Sumeru;
the asuras, non-Buddhists, and the hosts of māras of the six heavens of desire;
water, fire, wind, space, mountain forests, and cave dwellings.
Dwellings, palaces, and monasteries;
the great earth, rivers, streams, springs, and bathing pools;
temples, auspicious and inauspicious sites, and the assemblies of wandering deities.
They record all good and evil deeds with unimpeded supernatural power:
those who fly through the air on feathers and wings, the aquatic species with their scales,
the hairy and horned creatures, and all sentient beings, however small or sluggish.
The wandering souls in the wilderness whip the corpses in bitter agony;
for many lifetimes they have been bound by resentment and hatred, unable to escape.
Through kalpas, these vengeful spirits have exacted retribution for wealth and life.
Those deceased monks and nuns who had not yet realized the fruits of the path were mostly reborn as parents, kinsmen, or relatives;
by means of the Tathāgata’s teaching, they were able to escape the three miserable realms.
In immeasurable hells, they give rise to the bodhicitta;
each vows to relinquish and liberate themselves from the bonds of enmity,
and they praise and remember one another as they would think of their own parents.
Upon reaching this place of practice and realizing that [the Buddha] protects and mindfully remembers them, their hearts leap with joy;
it is as rare as encountering an udumbara flower.
This is due to their own past deeds performed while dwelling in the human realm.
The consciousness and emotions are difficult to stabilize and mostly arise following delusion;
accumulated as the source of suffering, they fail to attain the fruits of sainthood and instead give rise to afflictions and calamities.
Furthermore, dwelling upon the king’s land and water, they abide in the compassionate light of the Buddha;
constantly reflecting on past conditions, they still cherish the fruits of the present,
day and night reproaching themselves as to what extraordinary grace they might repay.
Among our retinues, relatives, parents, and kin, how many times have they ever betrayed us, turned against us, or become objects of inverted attachment?
How could we recognize them when their forms and faces have been changed?
We only pray that today, by virtue of this power of the Buddha, [we may see them as they truly are].
The carriage traveled afar through the void and arrived at this place of practice.
The compassionate light brushed against their bodies, each according to their own form and kind;
they washed away their worldly faults, gave rise to the bodhicitta, and accepted these offerings.
The Buddha told Ānanda: "If you wish to receive and uphold the dharma of offering food, you must rely upon the profound samādhi and the methods of the ācārya according to yoga.
This applies to those who delight in its practice."
One should learn from a yoga-ācārya how to generate the unsurpassed mind of great bodhicitta,
receive the samaya precepts, enter the great maṇḍala, and obtain empowerment.
However, one must first receive the empowerment of the five wisdoms of the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana and succeed to the rank of ācārya before it is permissible to transmit the teachings.
If it were not so, they would not grant one another permission;
even if one were to practice in such a manner, one would incur calamity and retribution for oneself,
committing the offense of stealing the Dharma, and ultimately achieve no merit or efficacy.
If one has received empowerment and, relying on the teacher’s instructions,
practices the yogic conduct and ritual procedures,
becoming well-able to discern and thoroughly comprehend the characteristics of phenomena.
Therefore, one is called a Tripiṭaka Ācārya only when one is able to transmit this teaching.
If one wishes to perform the ritual, one must first protect oneself, and the disciple should do likewise.
I know for certain that the sun has already selected a pure site:
a secluded garden amidst a magnificent mansion of refined essence,
where spirits and deities delight in flowing springs and bathing pools.
It may be located by rivers, streams, mountains, or marshes— places of merit—
or even within a hall or dwelling;
it should be properly plastered and smeared with fragrant clay and water.
According to the squareness, roundness, or size of the donor's means,
erect banners at the four corners and adorn them according to the ritual rules;
use five-colored silks to secure flaming jewels.
Furthermore, within the bead, one should install the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa, Mahākāruṇika, Sūtra-pratisarā, Uṣṇīṣavijayā,
and Mahākāruṇika; [specifically] the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa in the northeast and Mahākāruṇika in the southeast.
In the southwest is the Paritrāṇa;
in the northwest is the Uṣṇīṣavijayā.
Furthermore, the four pillars should be adorned according to the ritual rules.
This extraordinary and wondrously beautiful [substance] is named Auspicious Banner;
it establishes a boundary for a hundred yojanas, free from all decline and affliction, through the blowing of its scent,
the brushing of its shadow, the scattering of its dust, or the moistening by its water.
Karmic obstacles shall be extinguished and one shall obtain great benefit and merit;
all who see with their eyes or hear with their ears shall be universally benefited and saved.
Furthermore, hang silk streamers, banners, and canopies around the perimeter.
Jeweled fans and white whisks are arranged in their respective positions.

Next, regarding the sequence of the holy assembly for the altar ritual, the specific order is found in the instructional texts; one receives [the instructions] from the master concerning the *āgama* perfumed water, exquisite flowers, lamps, and ointments.
Regarding food, drink, medicinal decoctions, various fruit flavors, and other such items,
purify them according to the Dharma so that they are not defiled by impurities.
Once the preparations are complete, hold a fragrant incense burner in your hand.
Circumambulating the site of enlightenment to the right, he surveyed it with penetrating insight;
in any place that was not yet fully prepared, he made further adjustments and arrangements.
Once the adornments were complete, he [gathered] together with his disciples.
Having bathed in fragrant water and donned fresh, clean robes,
one goes outside to the central courtyard, where one sweeps and sprinkles according to the ritual;
then, one coats the ground with fragrant mud and decorates it according to the ritual.

This is called the Samaya-maṇḍala; it is the altar for bestowing the precepts upon disciples and spirits. Outside the ritual site (dojō), spread clean mats and cushions, maintain a dignified and solemn demeanor, and perform three prostrations.
Facing east, kneeling with the right knee on the ground and holding a censer in hand,
perform the rite of invocation.
Address the following to all the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Prajñāpāramitās, the Bodhisattvas, the Vajras, the Devas, and so forth:
And all the immeasurable noble ones of the various paths of action—
I now, through great compassion and riding upon the Buddha’s spiritual power, [speak].
I invoke all those within the three miserable realms and the various evil destinies throughout the entirety of the void in the ten directions,
including all hungry ghosts who have suffered from hunger and thirst for kalpas,
as well as the various officials of Yama and the celestial and terrestrial bureaucracies.
The karmic-path officials, Brahmans, and seers;
the spirits of those long deceased in the wilderness;
the various devas of the void and their retinues; and the diverse classes of ghosts and spirits.
I pray that all Buddhas, Prajñāpāramitā, Bodhisattvas, Vajra Devas, and the immeasurable sages and holy ones, as well as all the paths of karma,
will bestow their majestic radiance and increase their compassionate protection and mindfulness.
I universally pray that the celestial bureaus and earthly courts of the ten directions throughout the entirety of space, the officials of the karmic paths and the netherworld,
the immeasurable hungry ghosts, my parents from past lives,
and the long-deceased Brahmins and sages may all find peace.
All those bound by enmity and resentment who have deprived others of wealth and life,
along with various classes of spirits and deities of different species and their respective retinues, shall,
by the power of the Tathāgata, [be brought under control].
At dawn, at sunset, and during the hour of亥 (hai), the hosts of devas joyfully descend to perform miraculous manifestations;
they will certainly descend so that one may receive the supreme and wondrous flavor of the Tathāgata’s Dharma, the pure nectar of immortality.
Abundant food and drink nourish the field of the body;
merit and wisdom give rise to the aspiration for enlightenment (*bodhicitta*); forever departing from wrong conduct, one takes refuge in the Triple Gem;
practicing great compassion, one benefits all sentient beings.
Seeking the unsurpassed path, they do not undergo the various evil fruits of suffering within saṃsāra;
they are always born into noble families, free from all fears,
their bodies eternally pure, and they realize the unsurpassed path.
Having thus completed these threefold declarations,
one should then mentally offer incense, flowers, lamps,
and ointments to all the Buddhas, Prajñāpāramitā, Bodhisattvas, Vajradevas, and so forth.
To the immeasurable noble sages and all paths of karma:
I pray that you, out of compassion, descend and accept this meager offering.
Having prostrated three times, I pay homage.
Welcoming the assembly of noble ones into the inner altar, he circumambulates them three times to the right and returns to face east to pay homage to the assembly.

He then makes various offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, and unguents according to the ritual procedures. Following this, he reveals all his own transgressions and completes the rite of repentance.
Having returned the prostrations to the assembly of noble ones,
one should immediately apply scented paste to the palms using the *śīla-pāramitā* mudrā, direct the mind into meditative visualization, and only then perform the ritual procedure.
Next, form the *bhūmi-pradāraṇa-mudrā* (the seal for breaking through hell).
Form two vajra-fists; hook the thumbs and ring fingers together,
and extend the index and middle fingers, joining their sides.
Visualize opening the hells;
recite the mantra three times while pulling the cord three times.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo aṣṭābhyo devībhyo maitryai buddhakoṭibhyaḥ | Oṃ jyeṣṭhānubhāve dhiri dhiri hūṃ | By the power of this seal and mantra, [may there be success].
All the gates to the hells of every realm of existence shall open wide of their own accord through this seal-mantra.
Next, form the seal for summoning and inviting the hungry ghosts (preta).
The left wing forms the gesture of fearlessness;
the right wing is extended forward and upright.
The four [fingers] are slightly curved, performing the progression of the hook-summoning (*ākarṣaṇa*).
The mantra is: Oṃ jina-jike he he svāhā. Having thus performed the invocation, they all assembled like clouds.
With a mind of compassion, he praises and consoles them;
having caused them to rejoice, they come to thirst for the Dharma.
Next, he forms the mudrā for summoning transgressions.
Form the double-vajra-bind (*vajrabandha*) with both hands;
extend the thumbs and ring fingers like needles,
and bend the index and middle fingers like hooks.

The mantra for summoning sins is: Oṃ sarvapāpakarṣaṇa-viśodhana-vajrasattva-samaya hūṃ jaḥ. Next, form the mudrā for destroying sins: interlace the eight fingers with the palms facing inward; extend the *kṣānti* (ring) and *praṇidhi* (pinky) fingers as before. The mantra for destroying sins is: [as above].

Oṃ vajrapāṇi viṣphoṭaya sarvabāhyamardanani pramuñcaya sarvabāhyagati-vajra sarvasattva sarvatathāgata vajrasamaya hūṃ traṭ. Next, bind the seal of the fixed karma (*niyata-karma-mudrā*). With both hands in the *vajra-pāṇi* gesture, bend the second joints of the index fingers (*tarjanī*), and press the ring fingers (*anāmikā*) with the thumbs (*aṅguṣṭha*). The mantra for purifying karma is as follows:
Oṃ vajrakarma viśodhaya sarvavaraṇāni mudrasattvena samaya hūṃ. Fifth, this is the seal for repentance to extinguish transgressions.
Form the *vajrabandha* with both hands; bend the two joints of the thumbs and forefingers;

press the ring fingers and little fingers against the two middle fingers. The mantra for confession is: *Oṃ sarvapāpāni viśodhaya nātha vajrāya svāhā*. O sons of the Buddhas, having thus performed the confession—

Sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas are instantly and completely eradicated in a single thought-moment; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder. Next, to manifest the Tathāgata of Sublime Form and bestow the Amṛta Seal, rotate the left wrist forward.
The mantra for bestowing the nectar of immortality through the power of wisdom is as follows:
*Namaḥ surupāya tathāgatāya | tadyathā | oṃ suru suru prasu ru prasuru svāhā*. When reciting this mantra:
Visualize the syllable *vaṃ* above the seal of patience and aspiration;
from it flows the nectar-like Dharma-water of Prajñā,
which is sprinkled into the air.
All the various classes of hungry ghosts and spirits universally attained refreshing coolness;
their fierce fires were extinguished,
their physical bodies became moist and supple, and they were freed from the perception of hunger and thirst.
Next, perform the seal for opening the throat:
visualize a lotus flower held in the left hand;
with the right hand, snap the *kṣānti* and *dhyāna* fingers to produce a sound.
Play the lute while reciting [the mantra].
The mantra for opening the throat is as follows:
*Namo bhagavate vipulagātrāya tathāgatāya*. O sons of the Buddhas!
Now that I have bestowed this seal-mantra upon you,
your throats shall open of their own accord;
you will attain unimpeded penetration and be freed from all obstacles and difficulties.
O sons of the Buddha,
I now extol for you the auspicious names of the Tathāgatas,
which shall enable you to forever leave behind the sufferings of the three miserable realms and the eight difficulties.
Always being a true and pure disciple of the Tathāgata,
I take refuge in the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava. If there is a great assembly, let all the sons of the Buddha together recite this name.
If you hear the name of the Tathāgata Ratnavijaya, it can cause all the fires of your afflictions and karmic deeds to be completely extinguished.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vigatabhaya; as before, recite his name, and for those below, follow this same pattern.
O sons of the Buddha,
if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Free from Fear,
it shall enable you all to always attain peace and happiness.
Forever free from alarm and fear, pure and blissful.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vipulaśarīra.
O sons of the Buddha!
If you hear the name of the Tathāgata Vipula-kāya,
it shall cause the fiery flames of your karma as hungry ghosts with needle-like throats to cease burning and become cool and clear,
and the food and drink you receive shall have the flavor of nectar.
Homage to the Tathāgata Subhavarṇa-kāya.
All you sons of the Buddha,
if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Subhavarṇa-kāya, [you shall attain liberation].
It shall cause you all to avoid ugliness, to possess complete sensory faculties,
and to be endowed with the perfection of the marks and signs, most excellent and sublime in beauty,
being the foremost among gods and humans.
Homage to the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna.
O sons of the Buddha,
if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, [you shall attain liberation].
May it cause you all to be fully endowed with wealth and treasures,
so that whatever you require for your enjoyment shall be inexhaustible.
Homage to the Tathāgata Amitābha!
O sons of the Buddha:
if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Amitābha,
it can cause you all to be reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Born by transformation from a lotus flower, they enter the stage of non-retrogression.
Homage to the Tathāgata Universal Radiance of Vast and Majestic Power.
O sons of the Buddha!
If you hear the name of the Tathāgata Vast and Great Majestic Virtue, Sovereign Radiance,
it will enable you all to obtain five kinds of merit.
First, you shall be the most preeminent among all in the world.
Second, they attain the sublime and magnificent eyes of a bodhisattva.
Third, their majestic power is vast and surpasses all external paths and celestial māras,
like the sun illuminating the world.
Manifesting within the great ocean,
his merit is most lofty and sublime.
Fourth, he attains great mastery, such that whatever he directs is as he wishes.
It is like a bird flying through the sky without obstruction.
Fifth, one attains the great, firm radiance of wisdom;
body and mind are transparently clear, like a lapis lazuli bead.
O sons of the Buddha,
these seven Tathāgatas, by the power of their vows,
rescue sentient beings so that they may forever be free from afflictions.
They shall be liberated from the sufferings of the three miserable realms and abide in constant peace and bliss.
By reciting his name even once, one shall be freed from suffering for a thousand lifetimes and realize the Unsurpassed Way.
Next, I shall lead you all to take refuge in the Triple Gem.

"I take refuge in the Buddha, the Honored One among two-legged beings; I take refuge in the Dharma, the Honored One free from desire; I take refuge in the Saṃgha, the Honored One among assemblies. (Recite this three times.
"O sons of the Buddha, you have completed taking refuge in the Buddha; you have completed taking refuge in the Dharma; you have completed taking refuge in the Saṃgha. (Recite this three times.)
Relying upon the Triple Gem, you shall firmly protect and uphold the Dharma according to the teachings.
Next, for your sake, I shall arouse the bodhicitta;
listen attentively.
Form the vajra-palms with the *gñis-sbyor* (vajra-bond) gesture like lotus petals,
and place the seal upon the heart.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ mṛdityam utpādayāmi. Now that I have caused you all to generate the bodhicitta, O sons of the Buddha, you should know this.
The bodhicitta arises from great compassion;
it is the direct cause for attaining Buddhahood and the root of wisdom.
It is able to destroy ignorance, afflictions, and evil karma, and cannot be defiled or destroyed by them.
Next, I shall bestow upon you the Samaya-seal of the precepts.
Form the two hands into a fist, extending the *niṣṭhā* (ring) and *vara* (forefinger) fingers like needles.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ samayas tvaṃ. Now that the samaya-vow has been conferred upon you,
from this day forward,
it shall enable you...
Entering the stage of the Tathāgata,
they are true children of the Buddha;
born through transformation from the Dharma, they obtain a portion of the Buddha-dharma.
Next, bind the seal of the Tathāgata Amitābha (Immeasurable Majestic Virtue Sovereign Radiance). Visualize holding a vessel with the left fingers;
snap the fingers of the right hand in the *kṣānti-dhyāna* gesture.
Visualize that within the palm of the left hand there is the syllable *vaṃ*.
It flows forth as various kinds of immeasurable ambrosial food of the Dharma.
Then, recite the mantra for bestowing food:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatāvalokite vaṃ bala bala sambhara sambhara hūṃ. O sons of all the Buddhas!
Now that I have performed this seal-mantra for you all,
I shall transform this single meal into immeasurable food,
as vast as Mount Sumeru.
Its measure is equal to the dharma-realm and can never be exhausted.
Furthermore, with the previous seal, recite this mantra:
*Namo samanta-buddhānāṃ vaṃ*. O sons of the Buddhas!
I have now bestowed this seal-mantra (mudrā-mantra) upon you all.
By the power of the empowerment of this seal-mantra,
visualize that nectar flows forth from within the seal, forming an ocean of milk.
The flowing nectar permeates the Dharma-realm to universally deliver all sentient beings such as yourselves,
filling them completely and satiating them.
At that time, the practitioner takes the vessel of ambrosia with the right hand.

Facing east, one stands and pours [the water] onto the altar, or upon clean ground, or onto a large stone, or into a purified earthenware basin—also called an *ulambana* bowl—or even onto a raised platform; it may also be poured into a spring, pond, river, sea, or any flowing stream.
One must not discharge [excrement] beneath pomegranate or peach trees;
the ghosts and spirits will be terrified and unable to consume it.
